business_problem: DPVR wanted to turn AI glasses from a hardware novelty into a more useful and social intelligent product, but it needed real-time interaction, large-model services, and a scalable cloud foundation to move beyond standalone wearable features.
solution_summary: Baidu AI Cloud is supporting DPVR's move from VR hardware into AI glasses by combining real-time interaction services with large-model inference. The DPVR AI Glasses product uses Baidu's RTC real-time interaction solution together with Qianfan-based large models, including the DeepSeek-R1 and V3 series, so the glasses can respond to voice and contextual requests as a more conversational digital assistant. On Baidu's side, this is framed as an end-to-end AI-glasses support stack that spans lower-level infrastructure, higher-level application services, and the operational model required to keep iterating on wearable AI experiences. For DPVR, that means the glasses can shift toward natural-language interaction, contextual assistance, and more platform-like extensibility instead of behaving only as a display accessory. The same cloud base is intended to support future scenario innovation as the company explores what social and practical AI wearables should become.

solution_components.name: RTC Real-time Interaction Solution
solution_components.role: Provides the low-latency communication layer needed for live interaction on AI glasses.

solution_components.name: Qianfan Large Model Platform
solution_components.role: Supplies the large-model service environment behind the glasses' AI functionality.

solution_components.name: DeepSeek-R1 Model Service
solution_components.role: Contributes large-model reasoning capability to the wearable assistant experience.

solution_components.name: DeepSeek-V3 Model Service
solution_components.role: Supports general interaction and assistance scenarios in the glasses' AI stack.

data_flow: User requests from the glasses are transmitted through the RTC interaction layer into Qianfan-hosted model services, where DeepSeek models interpret intent and generate responses. The results are then returned to the wearable experience so DPVR can provide contextual assistance and conversational interaction through the glasses interface.
business_outcome: DPVR gained a cloud-backed AI layer for its glasses program, helping the company move faster toward more useful, social, and extensible wearable products instead of isolated hardware features.
metrics: DPVR reports more than 200 patents supporting its technology base.
architecture_clues: The glasses depend on both RTC interaction and cloud large-model services rather than embedding all intelligence on the device.
Baidu frames the offering as an end-to-end AI-glasses support stack spanning lower-layer infrastructure and upper-layer applications.
The solution is designed for future scenario expansion rather than only the first release of the product.
